ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence screening of every shareholder, director, officer, ultimate beneficial owner, settlement agent and payment counterparty against the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, UK HM Treasury OFSI Consolidated List (as extended to Bermuda), OFAC SDN List, EU Restrictive Measures, local Bermuda sanctions notices, and global PEP databases; continuous real-time and periodic 24/7 screening is required under the AML/ATF Act 2018, the AML/ATF Regulations 2018, and the BMA AML/ATF Codes of Practice, with risk-based enhanced due diligence (EDD) imposed upon identification of PEP, politically exposed, sanctioned, or high-risk-territory exposure. Bermuda has no material bilateral investment treaty with the payment corridor states; reliance is placed on the UK Overseas Territories investment protections and WTO/FATCA frameworks.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Bermuda Companies Registry e-Services (Registrar of Companies, Government of Bermuda, Ministry of Finance)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be registered in the English language using the Latin alphabet. Foreign-script or transliterated names are not accepted as the primary name unless accompanied by a registrar-approved English rendering. An exempted company name must end with 'Limited' or 'Ltd.' unless a statutory dispensation is granted, and must not be identical or confusingly similar to any name on the register or reserved-name index, and must not imply a prohibited or misleading relationship with the Government of Bermuda, the Crown, or any regulated sector. Distinctiveness is assessed against the full indexed corporate names database of Bermuda.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of an exempted company name, the applicant must file a written notice of appeal with the Registrar of Companies under Companies Act 1981 (as amended) within 14 days of the rejection notice, together with a search-output memorandum and a legal explanatory note demonstrating distinctiveness and non-conflict. The Registrar must issue an internal reconsideration decision within 14 business days; further administrative review may be sought from the Minister of Finance, with ultimate judicial review available in the Supreme Court of Bermuda. The applicant may submit an alternative reserved name in the same incorporation filing to avoid loss of priority and the 30-day reservation fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for a licensed cross-border payment service provider. Companies Act 1981 requires a physical registered office in Bermuda at a street address of a licensed CSP, distinct from the postal-only address; the BMA and the Economic Substance Act 2018 require a real and economic physical presence in Bermuda, including staff, premises, and board-management meetings, and a postal-only or virtual-office address is rejected for PSP licensing and economic substance attestation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High - approximately 75% likelihood of an unannounced BMA AML/CFT on-site inspection or verified physical-presence inspection within the first 18 months of incorporation/licensing, given the High_Risk_Special_License classification of the online merchant acquiring and clearing sector under Bermuda's National Risk Assessment and the BMA supervisory manual.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1981 (Bermuda), ss. 4-8 (Incorporation of Exempted Companies), s. 98 (Registered Office), and Second Schedule (Forms)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies and Partnerships Division, Government of Bermuda
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum of Association and Bye-Laws submitted together with Form EX-1 (Application for Registration of an Exempted Company)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; authorized share capital is fixed by the Memorandum of Association and may be denominated in any currency. No escrow account or capital deposit requirement applies to exempted companies under the Companies Act 1981.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) that the subscriber shares set out in the Memorandum of Association be and are hereby allotted and issued to the respective subscribers upon payment in full of the agreed consideration; (2) that the registered office of the Company be and is hereby fixed at the office of its licensed registered office provider in Bermuda pursuant to section 99 of the Companies Act 1981; (3) that [Name] be and is hereby appointed as the first Director and that [Name] be appointed as Company Secretary; and (4) that the said officers be jointly and severally authorized to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and file all applications and returns with the Registrar of Companies and the Bermuda Monetary Authority in connection with the Company's payment services licence and ongoing corporate compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies and Partnerships Division (name clearance desk)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name clearance application via the online e-Registry portal listing the proposed exempted company name (e.g. 'XYZ Cross-Border Payment Ltd'), ensuring the name ends with 'Limited' and is not misleading or identical to an existing registered name. Provide evidence of the reserved name upon approval.
required_dossiers: Certificate of good standing of parent entity (if any)
Business description covering payment gateway services
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to similarity or undesirability, the incorporators may resubmit an amended application with a new distinguishing name within 5 business days without additional statutory fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed corporate service provider and notary public in Bermuda
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum of Association (name, capital structure, subscriber details) and Bye-Laws (governance, board powers, indemnity, share transfer rules). Each subscriber executes the Memorandum in the presence of a witness, and the corporate service provider attests the execution and confirms compliance with the Companies Act 1981 for exempted companies.
required_dossiers: Letter of instruction from beneficial owners (including AML/KYC pack)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar or service provider queries the governance provisions (e.g. inadequate share transfer restrictions), amend the Bye-Laws and re-execute in counterpart; no statutory cure period is applied if the correction is filed within 14 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing with the Registrar of Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies and Partnerships Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed Memorandum of Association, Bye-Laws, Form EX-1, and the declaration of first directors and secretary via the e-Registry portal. Pay the filing fee of USD 1,740 and provide the registered office address in Bermuda. The Registrar examines the application against the Companies Act 1981 and the Bermuda Exempted Undertakings regime.
required_dossiers: Form EX-1 (Application for Registration of an Exempted Company)
Consent to act of first directors (Form EX-2)
Registered office consent from the service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition or query, the applicant must file a corrective filing or a letter of explanation within the statutory notice period (generally 21 days); failing which the application is deemed withdrawn and fees are partly forfeited.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Post-Incorporation Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies and the Company's registered office provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation. The corporate service provider then establishes the statutory registers (register of members, register of directors and officers, and register of charges), appoints the registered office, and files any necessary details with the BMA. The issuer of the certificate is the conclusive evidence of incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate contains a clerical error (wrong name or date), the Registrar will issue a Certificate of Rectification upon written application within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Exchange Control Authorization and BMA Regulatory Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For an exempted company with non-resident shareholders and payment-services activity, file the Exchange Control Application (Form EX-3) to obtain permission for the issue of shares to non-residents and to open bank accounts in foreign currency. Simultaneously, file the initial notification with the BMA Financial Institutions Supervision for the payment services licence application under the Payment Services Act 2022. This step is a precondition to lawful cross-border payment settlement operations.
required_dossiers: Business plan and projected transaction volumes
Payment Services Act 2022 licence application form
Ultimate beneficial owner register and corporate structure chart
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If exchange control consent is initially deferred or subject to conditions, the company may appeal to the BMA with a letter of representation and supporting transactional evidence for reconsideration within 14 days; further appeal lies to the Minister of Finance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Bermuda Monetary Authority (BMA), Financial Institutions Supervision, Payment Services Division
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Authorized Payment Institution Licence (Class A) under the Payment Services Act 2022 covering merchant acquiring, payment initiation, remittance, and settlement/clearing services on Visa, Mastercard, and Fedwire rails

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Planning in consultation with the Department of Environment and Natural Heritage (Bermuda Ministry of Home Affairs)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 4 - Not subject to a statutory Environmental Impact Assessment: office-based digital payment processing with no manufacturing, chemical, or physical discharge operations; EIA review is limited to leasehold fit-out and HVAC/electrical installations above regulatory floors.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance required with the Bermuda Water Authority trade effluent limits for sanitary wastewater; no point-source VOC or combustion emissions from software/data operations; electronic waste (servers, terminals, and card readers) must be handled by a licensed e-waste recycler under the Hazardous Waste Management Regulations and Basel Convention obligations; noise and thermal emissions from data-center equipment subject to local planning conditions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Bermuda Fire and Rescue Service under the Fire Safety Act 2015; building occupancy certificate from the Department of Planning confirming structural load capacity of the office premises; occupational health and workplace safety clearance under the Occupational Safety and Health Act 1982 covering electrical safety, emergency egress, and computer workstation ergonomics; business interruption and physical security review by the Bermuda Police Service for cash-equivalent handling areas.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Office of the Tax Commissioner within the Bermuda Ministry of Finance, administering payroll tax, customs duty, land tax and the Corporate Income Tax Act 2023; company incorporation and the Companies Register are administered by the Registrar of Companies in the Economic Development Department. Official information portal: www.gov.bm
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Bermuda does not issue a general income-tax TIN or VAT ID. The registration sequence for a foreign-owned exempted company is: (1) submit incorporation documents to the Registrar of Companies, including the exempted-company licence application and declaration of business activity, to obtain the Certificate of Incorporation and the unique Companies Register number (standard turnaround 1-2 business days); (2) if the entity employs staff, register as an employer with the Office of the Tax Commissioner and obtain the payroll-tax employer reference before first remuneration payment; (3) if the multinational group has global revenue of at least EUR 750 million, register for Bermuda corporate income tax and receive a CIT TIN, with a designation notice naming the responsible member and the ultimate parent identifier; (4) apply separately for non-resident exchange-control designation under the Exchange Control Act 1972 where unrestricted fund conversion is required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Bermuda has no check-the-box or transparent-entity election in its domestic law. Available elections are: (i) designation of the exempted company as non-resident for exchange-control purposes under the Exchange Control Act 1972; (ii) under the Corporate Income Tax Act 2023 for in-scope groups, elections over fiscal-year alignment, loss-utilisation mechanics, responsible-member designation, and the substance-based income exclusion; (iii) an election to apply the domestic minimum top-up tax so that Bermuda imposes the 15% effective minimum rate locally and preserves the group's control of the top-up allocation; (iv) elective treatment of distributions from segregated accounts or regulated investment structures where permitted by the Registrar.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: None - Bermuda has no VAT, GST or sales-and-use tax; the only indirect-style taxes are customs duties on imported tangible goods and the employer/self-employed payroll tax, neither of which applies to the cross-border payment-processing service turnover
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable for VAT/GST as no such regime exists. Payroll tax registration is mandatory for every Bermuda employer from the first dollar of Bermuda payroll, with a statutory annual payroll allowance for smaller employers; customs duty registration applies only to physical importers of goods. Cross-border service receipts by a Bermuda exempted company do not trigger any indirect-tax registration threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No electronic invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping or API-based fiscal reporting mandate applies in Bermuda. Service invoices for payment gateway fees are issued under the Companies Act 1981 and general contract law; customs duties on tangible imports are declared using the Bermuda Customs Department import procedures. No government e-invoice clearance platform exists for services.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable - Bermuda's indirect tax system contains no VAT, so no export zero-rating claim or refund mechanism exists for the cross-border payment gateway services. The gateway's interchange, processing and settlement fees are intangible services outside customs duty. If the group is in-scope for the Corporate Income Tax Act 2023, the 15% Bermuda corporate income tax applies to Bermuda-sourced income and to income attributable to a Bermuda permanent establishment, mitigated by the substance-based income exclusion; that is an income-tax charge, not an indirect export tax.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Not applicable - cross-border digital payment services require no Customs Export Declaration or bill of lading
For any ancillary tangible exports (e.g., POS hardware): commercial invoice, customs export declaration, and bill of lading or airway bill
Inward remittance certificates and bank settlement statements retained as transfer-pricing and economic-substance evidence for CIT audit purposes
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No indirect-tax clawback exists because no VAT is chargeable. The substantive clawback risk arises under the Corporate Income Tax Act 2023: inflated substance-based income exclusion claims, artificial transfer-pricing allocations, or false economic-substance declarations trigger penalties of up to BMD 250,000 per offence, reassessment of underpaid 15% corporate income tax with statutory interest, and possible revocation of the exempted-company licence or registration. Payroll tax arrears attract up to 30% penalties plus interest; unlicensed payment-activity in Bermuda additionally exposes the entity to Bermuda Monetary Authority enforcement measures.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Bermudian dollar is pegged at 1:1 to the United States dollar, and the BMA operates a fully convertible current and capital account framework. There are no general exchange controls restricting the conversion of BMD into USD or any other major currency. Profit remittance, dividend distribution, and capital repatriation are freely permitted for non-resident-owned exempted companies, subject only to compliance with the Anti-Money Laundering and Anti-Terrorist Financing regime administered by the BMA. Practical hurdles are limited to banking documentation and source-of-funds verification, not exchange control licensing. The payment gateway scope (merchant acquiring and clearing) attracts enhanced scrutiny under the Proceeds of Crime (Anti-Money Laundering and Anti-Terrorist Financing) Regulations, but no separate FX conversion permit is required for BMD/USD transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Bermuda imposes no statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio for the surrender of export proceeds. There is no equivalent to the territorial mandatory repatriation regimes found in certain emerging markets. Export receipts from a cross-border payment gateway may be held in any freely convertible currency, including USD, GBP, or EUR, in both Bermuda-licensed banks and approved offshore clearing accounts. The only relevant obligations arise from the BMA record-keeping and transaction monitoring requirements under the Anti-Money Laundering regime, requiring that all export or merchant settlement receipts be traceable, documented, and retained in accordance with the Proceeds of Crime Regulations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: The Bank of N.T. Butterfield & Son Limited

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low for locally licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs), Medium for internationally recognized offshore EMI services. Bermuda has not established a dedicated non-bank EMI licensing framework comparable to the UK FCA regime. Digital asset payment firms require a BMA Digital Asset Business license, and fiat-money EMIs may be treated as unlicensed financial service providers unless they register under the Banks and Deposit Companies Act or obtain a Money Service Business (MSB) license. Offshore EMIs such as Airwallex or a UK-licensed EMI can be used as ancillary transactional conduits, but the BMA-regulated banks remain the substantive high-risk PSP account solution. The legal constraint is that any EMI maintaining a domicile or place of business in Bermuda and operating payment services must obtain BMA authorization; simply operating through a foreign EMI without key management in Bermuda is viable but requires clear contractual separation and enhanced AML/KYC for the underlying merchant flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory for the natural-person directors and ultimate beneficial owners of a Bermuda Exempted Company seeking high-risk PSP banking. Remote or completely digital onboarding is not accepted by Tier 1 Bermuda commercial banks for this industry. At least one executive director and the majority of UBOs must attend an in-person meeting at the bank’s principal office in Hamilton, or at a recognized overseas branch with private-bank standards, prior to account finalization. Failing physical presence, a very limited remote path is available only if the company holds a licensed BMA relationship already and can produce a signed banker’s introduction from a top-20 global correspondent bank. In all cases, notarized certified passport copies, independent legal verification from a Bermuda counsel, and a registered agent’s certificate must accompany the applicant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: High-risk payment service provider/merchant acquiring business model with cross-border transactions to elevated-risk geographies; business uses ISO 6619 classification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide BMA-recognized PSP, MSB, or Digital Asset Business license or a definitive exemption letter; a detailed compliance manual covering customer due diligence, transaction monitoring, sanction screening, and suspicious activity reporting; merchant onboarding files with verified KYB/KYC; transaction flow diagrams; the annual external audit opinion on AML controls; and evidence of PCI DSS certification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Complex ownership structure of Bermuda Exempted Company, including nominee shareholders, trust ownership, or multiple interposed holding entities obscuring ultimate beneficial ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: File a current Certificate of Incumbency issued by the Bermuda registered agent; the Bermuda Beneficial Ownership Register filing confirmation; an organizational chart traversing to each natural-person UBO; copies of trust deeds or nominee agreements; statutory declarations from UBOs; and a legal opinion from Bermuda counsel confirming full transparency and power to bind the company.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Source-of-funds opacity for the initial capital injection and subsequent merchant settlement liquidity, particularly if funds originate from non-Bermuda offshore financial centers with high anonymity risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply audited or certified standalone financial statements of the monetizing controller; three to six months of bank statements showing the audit trail; notarized source-of-wealth declarations; tax filings or VAT registrations in the source jurisdiction; signed affidavits explaining the economic purpose of the capital injection; and confirmation that the injection passed through the Bermudian bank's pre-acceptance clearing account via a recognized SWIFT MT103 sender.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Sanctions and trade embargo exposure arising from the cross-border payment gateway's target merchant jurisdictions, especially if processing through Visa/Mastercard rails connects to sanctioned customers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Demonstrate a live sanctions screening solution (e.g., OFAC, EU, UN, and UK HM Treasury lists) with testing records; a sanctions risk management policy; merchant exclusion lists; geoblocking configuration in the payment gateway; country-specific compliance due diligence; and a written attestation by the compliance officer that no named sanctioned entity or jurisdiction is processed without a valid general or specific license.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for inbound capital uses SWIFT MT103 wire transfers in USD, GBP, EUR, or BMD-equivalent USD, transmitted through a U.S. correspondent clearing bank (e.g., JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Citibank) into the Bermuda bank’s nostro account. The wire must state a clear purpose code such as 'CFD – Financial Derivatives', 'LCS – Loans or Credits', 'SHS – Purchase of Shares', or 'ICJ – Inter-company Financing'. Beneficiary account name must match the exact registry name of the Bermuda Exempted Company, and the reference must include the board resolution approving the capital injection. The bank will require an instruction letter executed by two authorised signatories, a certified copy of the board resolution, and supporting legal documentation of the corporate capacity. For transactions exceeding a bank-defined threshold, usually USD 250,000, pre-matching of source-of-funds evidence and a beneficial ownership confirmation are mandatory before crediting the account. The funds remain subject to a 3–5 business day holding period pending BMA-required post-validation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound merchant settlements and trade disbursements are cleared through SWIFT MT103 priority payments, via the Bermudian bank's correspondent network, using Fedwire or CHIPS for USD, and CHAPS or Faster Payments for GBP. For commercial trade settlements involving goods or services, a documentary Commercial Letter of Credit (L/C) may be issued under UCP 600 for high-value disbursements above USD 100,000; the rail requires presentation of transport and insurance documents, commercial invoice, and compliant packaging lists. Bulk lower-value merchant payouts should be batched using ISO 20022 XML (pacs.008) messages to global acquiring banks, with unique transaction references and hashed merchant IDs. Every outbound disbursement is subject to real-time OFAC/HM Treasury sanctions screening and transaction monitoring; non-standard counterparties will trigger additional AML review for up to 48 hours. Recurrent payouts require an approved beneficiary list and a standing instruction with reference to the payment gateway merchant agreement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/BMD outright foreign exchange forwards (or zero-cost collars) to manage near-term settlement liquidity and the 1:1 peg stability
GBP/USD deliverable foreign exchange forwards for converting UK-origin merchant revenue into USD settlement pools
EUR/USD non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for preserving existing USD liquidity without requiring euro delivery when processing EU merchants
Cross-currency interest rate swaps between USD and GBP to hedge the funding mismatch between the Bermuda treasury account and operational GBP clearing balances
Plain vanilla currency swaps for tenor-matched hedging of capital injection repayment and dividend remittance liabilities arising from the cross-border gateway

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% — Bermuda imposes no corporate income tax on a tax-exempt Exempted Company. Payroll Tax and Social Insurance apply only to locally engaged employees. A 15% minimum tax under the Corporate Income Tax Act 2024 applies solely to constituent entities of MNE groups with consolidated revenue of EUR 750M or more.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 0% effective rate. Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act 1966 certification guarantees no income, capital gains, or dividend taxes until 31 March 2035. No statutory CIT holidays or preferential deductions exist because no CIT base exists.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No CIT return exists. Filings: (1) Annual Return under Companies Act 1981 via Bermuda Registry e-Filing (roc.gov.bm / Bermuda Online Registry); (2) ESR Annual Return via Bermuda Tax Authority e-Filing (IRIS/BTA portal); (3) PSP annual compliance return under National Payment Systems Act 2020 via BMA portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (Annual Return and ESR Return); monthly or quarterly (Payroll Tax and BMA prudential returns where applicable).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual Return: within 30 days after the incorporation anniversary (return date). ESR Return: within 6 months after the accounting period end. Payroll Tax: by the 15th day of the month following each month or quarter end. BMA returns: as directed by the PSP licence conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Annual Return — Part A: Company Information
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered name, company number, registered office, principal place of business, directors and officers, shareholders, share capital, and exempted status declaration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter non-resident directors and shareholders with passport or ID and country of residence only; do not assert U.K. or Bermuda tax residence. No U.K. NI numbers required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Annual Return — Part B: Local Business Declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration that the company has conducted all business outside Bermuda and holds no Bermuda business licence.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm all PSP gateway activity is executed abroad, with no Bermuda permanent establishment, local office, or local merchant solicitation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: ESR Return — Income and CIGA Schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Relevant income, core income-generating activities, employees, premises, and board-meeting substance indicators.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A pure third-party PSP outside the ESR relevant-activity list files a nil substrate; group-affiliated treasury or payment services must evidence Bermuda CIGA.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late Annual Return: default fine up to BDA $200 plus daily fines; ESR filing failure: up to BDA $10,000 plus BDA $10,000 per continuing day; BMA late-return fines imposed by licence enforcement action.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% — no dividend withholding tax, no remittance tax, and no capital gains tax on Exempted Company distributions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Not applicable: Bermuda has no comprehensive double taxation agreements. Only Tax Information Exchange Agreements (TIEAs) exist, including with the United Kingdom; these do not grant withholding relief and no TRC submission protocol applies. Shareholder-level taxation is solely a matter of the recipient's residence jurisdiction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% statutory on outbound royalties and interest; no treaty reduction is available given the absence of DTAs. Outbound flows remain exposed to the payee's domestic CFC and diversionary rules (e.g., U.K. CTA 2010 Part 9A).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Not applicable — Bermuda has no statutory transfer-pricing legislation or Local File/Master File threshold. ESR requires contemporaneous substance documentation for relevant activities; MNE groups within the Corporate Income Tax Act 2024 must file OECD GloBE information returns where group revenue is EUR 750M or more.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations 2018: relevant activities (banking, insurance, shipping, fund management, financing/leasing, headquarters, distribution/service centre, IP) must demonstrate CIGA in Bermuda. A pure merchant-acquiring PSP serving unrelated merchants is generally outside the list; intra-group treasury, settlement, or service-centre activity is in scope. Non-compliance: BDA $250,000 fine, automatic TIEA exchange, and strike-off.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating cross-border merchant acquiring, clearing, settlement, or payment-gateway services without the required licence under the National Payment Systems Act 2020, or acting beyond the BMA licence scope.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal offence: summary conviction fine up to BDA $100,000 or imprisonment up to 2 years, or both; on indictment, fine up to BDA $250,000 or imprisonment up to 10 years, or both; the BMA may additionally levy administrative financial penalties and revoke the licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may be prosecuted as participants; the corporate veil is pierced where the company is a mere façade; the BMA may issue prohibition directions and the Supreme Court may impose travel bans and disqualification orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Abuse of EUTP Exempt Status
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Exempted Company as a shell to divert U.K. corporation tax or customer-jurisdiction taxes while the payment gateway is genuinely managed and controlled (brain management) from the United Kingdom, creating a de facto U.K. PE.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Tax Exemption Certificate is void if local business is conducted; the company may be struck off. Foreign tax authorities apply GAAR and CFC rules: relevant profits revert to the U.K. at the 25% corporation tax rate with penalties and interest; TIEA exchanges are triggered by ESR substance failures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a sham arrangement face civil restitution, disqualification under Companies Act 1981, and fraudulent-trading liability; HMRC may lift the veil against a controlling-mind director for the underlying U.K. tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing nil ESR returns while performing in-scope relevant activity — e.g., intra-group treasury settlement, payment-float financing, or group service-centre functions — without Bermuda employees, premises, CIGA, or board direction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Economic Substance (Substance Requirements) Act 2018: non-compliance penalty up to BDA $10,000 plus BDA $10,000 per day; failed substance test: fine up to BDA $250,000 with automatic exchange of information with U.K. and TIEA partners; persistent default leads to winding-up.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors sign the substance declaration and are personally liable for knowingly false certification; the Supreme Court may order personal payment of penalties, impose travel bans, and disqualify directors; corporate indemnity is void for fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing card-not-present and cross-border third-party payouts without full CDD/KYC, beneficial-ownership checks, transaction monitoring, SAR filing to the FIAU, and sanctions screening, in breach of the AML Act 2008 and Proceeds of Crime Regulations 1998.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: BMA financial penalty up to BDA $1,000,000 per contravention; money-laundering conviction: imprisonment up to 14 years; sanctions breach: fine and imprisonment up to 7 years; PSP licence revoked with immediate effect.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Senior management is strictly accountable to the BMA: individual fines, prohibition orders, public censure; directors may be charged for consenting or conniving in laundering; travel bans and asset sequestration are available; veil-piercing applies where the PSP is used as a fraud conduit.
